deductions: Continuity: “See Qualify and close, Lead scanning app, and On the day” points to three destinations without distinguishing the immediate next step.
Clarity: “14–15 Oct Wednesday and Thursday exhibition days” and “1 goal relevant conversations” read like labels with missing punctuation.
Tightness and organisation: “Before the visitor leaves: agree who will do what and when” repeats the close instruction in section 03.
Continuity: The section ends after “bring in the right M2M specialist” without pointing the reader to the conversation guidance in section 02.
Clarity: “qualified, owned follow-up” is less concrete than the ownership process explained in section 03.
Tightness and organisation: “relevant conversations” repeats the brief’s goal without adding much at that point.
Actionability: “Focus on emergency services, government fleets, utilities and remote operations” names priorities but gives no tie-breaker when several visitors need attention.
Continuity: The handover guidance says to “record the exact question” but leaves the recording method to later sections without a pointer.

Clarity: “when their expertise helps” in section 01 becomes specific here, but “other product, carrier, partner or technical questions” leaves the Peplink versus other-partner split slightly hard to parse.
Tightness and organisation: The final “Products and demonstrations” paragraph is an internal distribution gate inside otherwise rep-facing talk guidance.
Actionability: “ask Eerin or Gajan if they are available” gives no direct handover step when one is present.
Continuity: “A relevant action is a visitor-requested follow-up” narrows the earlier rule to agree what M2M will do; a visitor could accept an M2M-proposed action without requesting it.
Clarity: “records without a clear owner” appears before the explanation that Peter and Eerin assign owners after the debrief.
Tightness and organisation: “Before the visitor leaves, agree what M2M will do and when” repeats the brief’s close instruction.
Actionability: The “visitor-requested follow-up” definition could cause reps to omit an agreed action proposed by M2M from the assignment workflow.
Continuity: “Sales leadership to confirm” interrupts the scan-to-failure-recovery sequence.
Clarity: “Cameron Walsh is the stand contact for operational issues” does not specify whether a failed scan should go to Cameron before or after the registration desk.
Tightness and organisation: “Press SUBMIT after every scan” and “Press SUBMIT before starting the next conversation” repeat the same save rule.
Actionability: The failed-scan path names the registration desk for app support but does not say what the rep should do if scanning remains unavailable.

overall_findings: The draft does not pass: section 03 falls below 95 on continuity and actionability because its definition of a relevant action may exclude an agreed follow-up.
The visible text retains the section 04 SUBMIT instruction and contains no named customer or project, unapproved count or outcome, or visible contradiction of the confidentiality rule.
Section 05 is outside this pass; its roster and timetable were not supplied for a preservation check.
